skill.name: nano-banana-builder
skill.description: Build Next.js image generation applications with Google Gemini Nano Banana models, including server actions, image editing flows, storage, rate limits, and deployment patterns.
skill.summary: Create production-ready Gemini image generation apps with model selection, storage, editing, and rate-limit guidance.
skill.author: CesarAugustusGroB

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many template literals, environment variable examples, placeholder URLs, and documentation snippets. Manual review found these are instructional examples for Gemini image apps, not command execution, secret exfiltration, or prompt injection. No net-new semantic security findings were identified.

content.value_statement: Image generation apps need correct model names, server-side API use, storage, and quota handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through production-ready Nano Banana app patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains the exact Gemini image model names to use for Nano Banana and Nano Banana Pro.
Provides Next.js server action and API route patterns for image generation and editing.
Shows React client patterns for generators, galleries, iterative editors, and batch workflows.
Covers object storage options using Vercel Blob and S3-compatible services.
Includes rate limiting, caching, error handling, and cost optimization guidance.
limitations: It is documentation and examples, not a runnable application by itself.
Model availability, pricing, and quotas must be verified against current Google documentation.
Storage and rate-limit examples need project-specific authentication and deployment setup.
Generated code still requires security review before production use.

use_cases.title: Launch an image generator
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js app that turns prompts into images with the correct Gemini image model and server-side API calls.

use_cases.title: Add iterative image editing
use_cases.description: Build a conversational editor that keeps image history and lets users refine outputs through natural language.

use_cases.title: Prepare production operations
use_cases.description: Plan storage, rate limits, caching, and user-friendly error handling before opening the tool to more users.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic generator
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-builder to create a simple Next.js image generator with gemini-2.5-flash-image and a clear loading state.

prompt_templates.title: Add storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-builder to add Vercel Blob storage to my Gemini image generator and return saved image URLs.

prompt_templates.title: Build iterative editing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-builder to design an iterative image editor with conversation history, image upload, and explicit edit actions.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for production
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nano-banana-builder to review my image app for rate limits, storage choices, caching, error handling, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: Build a prompt-to-image app for marketing thumbnails.
output_examples.output: A Next.js implementation plan with server-side generation, model selection, prompt form, gallery display, and storage recommendations.

output_examples.input: Add editing to an existing generated image workflow.
output: A conversational editing flow that keeps prior image context.
A client component with explicit edit submission.
Server guidance for passing image data safely.

output_examples.output: A checklist covering rate limits, object storage, cached results, environment variables, user feedback, and retry behavior.

best_practices: Keep API keys on the server and expose generation through server actions or API routes.
Use the fast model for drafts and the pro model for final quality or text-heavy images.
Add explicit submit actions, loading states, storage, and rate limits before production release.
anti_patterns: Do not invent Gemini model names or add date suffixes to image model identifiers.
Do not generate images on every keystroke because it wastes quota and slows the app.
Do not store large base64 images directly in the database for production workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Next.js applications that generate, edit, store, and display images using Gemini Nano Banana models.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include complete production code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. You still need to adapt and test the code in your project.

faq.question: Does it require API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Real applications need server-side Gemini credentials and optional storage or Redis credentials.

faq.question: Can it help with image editing workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for multi-turn editing, image history, and natural language refinement.

faq.question: Is it only for Vercel?
faq.answer: No. It includes Vercel Blob examples and S3-compatible storage patterns for other deployments.
